newsitem.title: UK: T-bonds steady in London, auction outlook upbeat.
newsitem.headline: T-bonds steady in London, auction outlook upbeat.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries trod water in quiet London trade on Wednesday ahead of what dealers said would likely be a fairly upbeat 10-year auction later.
Chase bond salesman Charles Quigley said early weakness in the dollar against the yen had tempted some Japanese investors into the Treasury curve, but he added volume overall was fairly low.

The dollar slipped beneath 125 yen earlier, shaken by a report from Japanese news agency Kyodo that the G3 was exploring the possibility of joint intervention in forex markets to sell dollars for yen.
"There's been some derivative interest emerging in the five year sector -- I understand one or two large corporate bond issues are in the pipeline this morning," Quigley said.
By 1007 GMT, the 30-year long bond was at 96-17, unchanged from Tokyo and down from 96-21 at the New York close. Five-year paper was at 100-09, unchanged from both Tokyo and New York.
Quigely said the auction of $12 billion of 10-year paper later should be reasonably well received, despite the luke warm response to Tuesday's three-year auction.
Julius Baer senior economist Dick Howard agreed.

"The three-year didn't perform particularly well because people were fearful of a rate hike on May 20," he said. "But a tightening wouldn't be that bad for the longer end, it would suggest the Fed is being pre-emptive, so I'd expect a better response in the 10-year auction."
Howard said the Fed's Beige Book, due at 1800 GMT, may have a positive impact on the market. The Beige Book gives anecdotal evidence of business conditions around the country.

"People have been starting to talk about some signs of a slowdown in the U.S. economy," he said. "The Beige Book has not really changed its message for some time so if there is some phrase to the effect that in some areas expansion may be slowing, that should be positive for the market.

First quarter productivity and unit labour costs are due at 1400 GMT. Labour costs are seen up 1.0 percent from a 2.5 percent rise previously. March wholesale inventories are due at 1400 GMT and are seen up 0.4 percent. March consumer credit, due at 1900 GMT, is forecast at $6.7 billion.
June T-bond futures were down 6/32 at 109-29 by 1023 GMT.
